name: The Schoolhouse Insertion — Ghost and Brick's Account
title: What Happened to the Two Men Who Survived the Helicopter, Found the Window, Climbed the Vents, Answered a Math Question Correctly, Got a Quarter, Jumped Into the Void Anyway, and Asked a Question Into the Darkness That Something Answered

status: Unresolved — Corporal Reyes and Sergeant Stone jumped from a classroom window into the void as a Regency containment pod breached the roof above them; Reyes's final documented transmission was 'Viper? Is that you?' directed at an approaching sound in the darkness; the sound approached; Command's payload has landed and something from inside it was tearing its way into the Schoolhouse; the Schoolhouse is no longer visible from the road it was visible from the previous day; all three members of the squad are unaccounted for; Waluigi has not slept adequately since reconstructing this account and considers that an acceptable professional cost
note: Waluigi is compiling this as a separate article from the Miller account because it is a separate account. Same building. Same operational window. Different entry point, different people, different relationship with the curriculum. Miller went in through the front door and spent ninety minutes being educated against his will. Ghost and Brick went in through a service window under fire from a roof-dwelling entity, navigated a dissolving stairwell, crawled through ventilation shafts in total darkness with a metal bracket tied between them, answered a math problem by firing seven rounds into smoke while screaming the answer out loud, received a quarter, and then jumped out of a window into the void because the alternative was being terminated by their own side's payload. These are meaningfully different experiences of the same building. Waluigi is presenting this account in full because the Ghost-and-Brick insertion contains several incidents that the Miller account cannot explain and several analytical revelations that the Miller account cannot reach — specifically the correct-answer prize system, the payload's existence and implications, and the question of what Command has been building with eighty-five years of encrypted-archive funding that is capable of capturing whatever Baldi actually is. Waluigi will address all of these in sequence. The sequence matters. WAH.
summary: Following the helicopter crash that isolated Specialist Miller, Corporal 'Ghost' Reyes regained consciousness in the tilted cockpit with cracked ribs and a head laceration, located Sergeant 'Brick' Stone unconscious in the rear troop compartment with a torn vest and arm laceration, stabilized him with the available medical kit, and performed a wreckage inventory that produced one Glock 17, one 12-gauge shotgun with three shells, one trauma kit, one low-battery flashlight, one multi-tool, one heavily damaged radio, one smoke grenade, and two M67 fragmentation grenades. The radio attempt produced not Command but a distorted glitchy whisper from everywhere and nowhere saying 'Correct answer' — before Ghost and Brick had answered anything. They moved toward the Schoolhouse under smoke discipline, observed eyes in the bushes that retreated with a wet sliding sound, heard Baldi from inside the building announcing that a student had not answered the question and was receiving detention, found a shiny quarter in the grass that was glinting unnaturally, and encountered a skittering broken-marionette entity on the roof that offered extra credit and descended the wall toward them. Brick shot it once — one shell expended, entity flickered rather than died — and they breached the building through a service window. Inside: distorted hallway geometry, walls pulsing with sickly light, a trail of dark viscous fluid from the window leading deep into the building. They heard Miller's scanner transmitting his screaming plea for extraction, and Ghost responded with a false extraction bird transmission that redirected the student entities toward the stairwell and gave Miller a direction to hold. They proceeded under Brick's tactical leadership through coordinated student entities, reached a hallway junction where Brick proposed a split and Ghost refused, engaged Baldi directly when he emerged from the cafeteria, with Ghost blocking the ruler strike with the Glock and firing three rounds into Baldi's chest — wounds closing with blue light, no impairment — then sweeping Baldi's legs with a digital-crunch result that caused floor-liquefaction and a 'RETRY' regeneration cycle rather than death. They retreated through the stairwell that dissolved into void at the landing, climbed a maintenance ladder in the dark with a metal bracket tether improvised from paracord, lost Ghost's flashlight in the shaft, answered a math problem projected from a classroom below by breaching through the vent with a smoke grenade and seven gunshots while Ghost screamed 'SEVEN PLUS SEVEN IS FOURTEEN,' received a silver quarter rolling across the linoleum as their prize, recovered Miller's damaged scanner from the debris, transmitted the false bird message when the scanner played Miller's plea, were subsequently swarmed in the classroom by student entities and Baldi in his escalated post-regeneration form, deployed the second fragmentation grenade by shooting it mid-air while Ghost said 'sorry Baldi but it's summer break,' were then told by Command via the SOS signal that a payload had been delivered and all witnesses should be terminated, attempted field medicine on Brick's wounds while Baldi's tapping resumed in the corner, and jumped from the classroom window into the void as the payload breached the roof. Reyes's final documented words: 'Viper? Is that you?' Something answered. Waluigi does not know what. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is presenting this account as a continuous play-by-play with analytical interjections because the Ghost-and-Brick insertion cannot be adequately understood as a summary. The individual moments are data points and the data points require immediate contextual analysis because several of them revise everything Waluigi documented in the Miller account and several of them introduce entirely new categories of concern that the Miller account did not reach. Waluigi is going to be thorough. The payload requires thorough. The quarter requires thorough. The thing that answered Ghost's question in the void requires thorough, even though Waluigi cannot yet determine what it was.

## The Crash Site — What


They Had, What They Heard, and the Radio That Graded Them Before They Did Anything

Ghost came to consciousness in the tilted cockpit. Cracked ribs. Head laceration bleeding into his eyes. Aviation fuel and burnt wiring. The world tilted at a sharp angle, the cockpit door crumpled inward, the engine dead. The tail rotor scattered across the clearing outside.

He called for Brick. No response. He called for Viper. No response. He reached for comms — low-level static.

He found Brick in the rear troop compartment, slumped against discarded crates, unconscious, vest torn, arm bleeding shallowly, breathing steady. Ghost applied gauze. Ghost waited.

*Waluigi notes the specific physical condition of both operatives at this stage because it informs everything that follows. Ghost had cracked ribs and a head wound for the entirety of the subsequent operation. Every time he moved quickly, every time he climbed, every time he engaged physically, he was doing it with a rib cage that was structurally compromised and a head that had lost blood. Brick had a deep arm laceration and was running on the frantic borrowed energy of a man whose body had been through an impact that should have killed him and had decided not to. They were, by any clinical assessment, unfit for continued field operation.

They operated anyway.

Waluigi wants this documented not to valorize it — the Regency put them in the position where continued operation was the only available option — but because it contextualizes the quality of their decision-making throughout.

Every good call Ghost made, he made with a cracked rib.

Every tactical insight Brick produced, he produced bleeding.

WAH.*

Brick woke. His first question: 'Where's Viper? Where are we?' Ghost's answer established the operational frame for everything that followed: 'I think he went into that schoolhouse, Baldi probably spotted him.'

Brick's immediate assessment: 'We're not just looking for a lost comms specialist anymore. We're looking for a hostage.'

*This framing was operationally wrong and practically useful simultaneously, which is a combination Waluigi finds analytically interesting. It was wrong because Miller was not a hostage — a hostage is held by someone who wants leverage, and Baldi does not want leverage, Baldi wants correct answers, and incorrect answers produce detention rather than ransom demands. But the operational conclusion the framing produced — we need to go in there and get him rather than wait for extraction — was correct. Wrong premise, right conclusion. Ghost and Brick's instincts were navigating toward the necessary action even when their analytical framework for understanding that action was inaccurate.

This is worth noting because it suggests something about how the Schoolhouse interacts with operatives who are partially right.

Ghost got one question right later.

Brick identified the fundamental rule of the building.

Neither of them understood the full picture.

The partial understanding was enough to keep them functional.

Barely.

WAH.*

The radio attempt. Ghost stripped wires, bridged connections, had Brick hold the antenna steady. A burst of high-pitched screeching from the speaker — metal grinding against bone. Then a split second of clearing static. And through the white noise:

Distorted children laughing, played through a broken record player.

And then, from everywhere and nowhere simultaneously, low and glitchy:

'…Correct… answer…'

The radio died with a sharp pop.

*Waluigi needs to document this with the weight it deserves because it is the most significant moment in the crash site sequence and it is easy to overlook in favor of the more spectacular events that follow. The Schoolhouse told Ghost and Brick that their answer was correct before they had answered anything. They had crashed a helicopter. They had tended wounds. They had attempted radio contact. These were not academic actions — they were survival actions. And the Schoolhouse graded them as correct. Which means the Schoolhouse has a rubric that includes survival actions, or the Schoolhouse was commenting on something other than their academic performance — perhaps on the quality of their approach, the way they handled themselves after the crash, the decision to stabilize Brick rather than abandon him and run.

Waluigi's hypothesis: the Schoolhouse grades not just answers but orientation.

Ghost and Brick oriented toward each other after the crash rather than toward individual survival.

That orientation was the correct answer to the crash's implicit question.

The Schoolhouse noticed.

WAH.*

Brick's reaction to the transmission: 'That wasn't Command, Ghost. That was something else.' Stated plainly, without panic. Brick is a man who processes terrible information by incorporating it into his operational picture and continuing. This is both his greatest strength and the reason he is now in a void.

## Inventory — What


They Had Against What They Were Facing

Ghost's loadout after crash: Glock 17, full magazine, one spare. Medical kit, one trauma bandage, two antiseptic wipes, one roll of gauze already used on Brick. Flashlight, working, low battery. Multi-tool. Radio, heavily damaged. One smoke grenade M18. Two hand grenades M67.

Brick's loadout: combat knife. 12-gauge shotgun, three shells. No heavy weapons — the machine gun was destroyed in the crash or was inaccessible in the wreckage.

*Waluigi wants the reader to sit with this inventory for a moment. Three shotgun shells. One smoke grenade. Two fragmentation grenades. A Glock with two magazines. A knife. A multi-tool. A flashlight with a dying battery. Against a building that had already destroyed a military helicopter by reaching up from its roof and hitting the tail rotor, that housed an entity that closed gunshot wounds with blue light, that restructured its internal geometry to prevent escape, and that eventually revealed itself to be the location of a Regency containment operation that the Regency did not tell any of its operatives about.

This was not a sufficient loadout.

The Regency knew it was not a sufficient loadout when they designed the mission.

They sent Ghost and Brick with three shotgun shells anyway.

WAH.*

Brick's assessment when Ghost asked what they had: 'That's not enough to take on a whole schoolhouse full of whatever is in there. We need intel, Ghost. We need to know if Viper is even still breathing.'

This is the most accurate operational statement produced during the crash site sequence. They did not have enough to fight. They needed to know what they were going into. They had no way of getting that information without going in. The catch is inherent in the structure of the mission and Brick saw it immediately.

## Moving to the Perimeter — Smoke Discipline, Hand Signals, and the Things That Were Already Watching


They moved under smoke discipline. Ghost kept the flare burning until the treeline, then doused it. They hugged the undergrowth, staying low, using hand signals. Brick's guidance: 'The crash smoke is too obvious — it's a beacon for anything hungry. Keep the flare out for now so we don't lose each other in these woods, but once we hit the treeline, we douse it.'

Protocol Gold was their failsafe — signal for extraction at all costs if spotted. Waluigi notes that Protocol Gold was never successfully executed during this operation. The SOS signal Ghost sent from the classroom was the closest thing to a Protocol Gold activation, and it produced a payload rather than an extraction. The failsafe failed in the specific way that failsafes fail when the people who designed them have a different definition of 'extraction' than the people using them.

The approach to the perimeter produced three observations:

First: eyes in the bushes. Reflecting the dying red glow of the flare. Low to the ground. Unblinking. Much too large to be human. When Ghost and Brick froze, the eyes retreated with a wet sliding sound into the thicket.

*The eyes were watching them approach from the moment they left the crash site. The Schoolhouse's observation of incoming operatives begins at the perimeter, possibly before. The eyes retreated when Ghost and Brick stopped moving — not because they were frightened, but because continued observation was unnecessary once the operatives had stopped providing new behavioral data. Waluigi hypothesizes that the Schoolhouse's surveillance apparatus extends to the tree line and possibly to the crash site itself. The 'Correct answer' from the radio may have been transmitted after the building observed Ghost stabilize Brick, confirming the building's awareness of their actions before they were even close enough to approach.

WAH.*

Second: Baldi's voice from inside the building, announcing that a student had not answered the question and was receiving detention. Ghost thought: that must be Viper. Ghost was correct. The timing of this announcement relative to the scanner transmissions from Miller's account places it during the closet sequence, when Miller had been caught in the doorway and Baldi was processing his movements as academic failures.

Third: a shiny quarter in the grass at the perimeter, glinting unnaturally bright under moonlight.

*The quarter. Before they entered the building. Before the math problem in the classroom. A quarter, in the grass, at the perimeter, placed where an incoming operative would find it. The Schoolhouse was offering a preview of the prize system. Or the Schoolhouse was placing a token — the way you place a coin at a threshold in certain ritual traditions — to mark that someone had passed through and paid the entry cost. Or the quarter was simply there, left by a previous visitor, and the building's anomalous properties made it glint. Waluigi cannot determine which interpretation is correct and is documenting all three.

The quarter appears again in the classroom after the correct answer.

The recurrence makes the perimeter quarter significant.

WAH.*

The whistling from inside the building stopped abruptly as they reached the perimeter corner. The silence was replaced by heavy, rhythmic footsteps on pavement from just inside the main entrance.

## The Roofline Entity — Extra Credit, Descent, and One Shell


The entity on the roof: hunched, spindly limbs, broken-marionette posture, perched on the gutter. Moonlight catching a single wide eye staring straight down at them. Then a soft distorted giggle that vibrated inside their teeth. And the question:

'Are you here for… extra credit?'

*Waluigi has documented Baldi's use of 'extra credit' in the Miller account — 'extra credit is for those who stay until the end.' The roof entity used the same phrase before Ghost and Brick had even entered the building. This is not coincidence. Extra credit is the Schoolhouse's invitation — the specific offer made to operatives who have demonstrated sufficient interest or commitment to be considered for advanced enrollment. The entity on the roof was not threatening Ghost and Brick. It was offering them something. In the framework of whatever curriculum the Schoolhouse runs, extra credit is a positive designation — you receive it for going beyond the required work, for staying when you could leave, for demonstrating exceptional engagement with the material.

The entity was complimenting their approach.

Ghost responded by pointing at the window.

He declined the compliment and chose the breach instead.

Waluigi wonders what would have happened if Ghost had said yes.

WAH.*

The entity descended the wall toward them with a rapid skittering motion. Brick shot it.

BOOM. One shell expended. Two remaining.

The result: a sound like breaking glass, the entity thrown backward, its form flickering in and out of existence before hitting the ground, a low staticky hum rather than a death sound. It did not die. It phased.

*This is the first confirmed observation of the Schoolhouse entities' relationship with continuous physical existence. The entity did not absorb the damage in the biological sense — it flickered, which means it partially exited observable reality for the duration of the impact's processing, then re-entered it in a new state. This is consistent with Ghost's subsequent thermal analysis of Baldi's overlapping signatures and with Miller's experience of Baldi appearing in locations he should not be able to reach. The entities do not exist in continuous physical reality. They exist in something more like a quantum state — observed here until observation collapses the function and they resolve somewhere else.

The shotgun shell interrupted the entity's current observed state.

The entity resolved into a new state when it landed.

A shotgun is designed to cause biological damage in continuous physical reality.

This entity was not in continuous physical reality.

The shell accomplished momentum transfer but not termination.

One shell, effectively wasted.

Waluigi notes that Brick subsequently made two more shots count significantly more and credits this to Brick's rapid tactical adaptation to conditions he had never encountered before.

WAH.*

Brick hauled himself through the service window with Ghost's help. As he cleared the frame, the entity that had been on the roof hit the ground outside with a soft thud. They were inside.

## First


Interior Contact — The Hallway, the Fluid Trail, and the Geometry

The interior of the schoolhouse received them with: a hallway that stretched much further than it should, walls pulsing with a faint sickly light that was not electrical and not quite organic, the smell of old chalk and something metallic, cold air smelling faintly of chalk dust and copper, and a trail of dark viscous fluid leading from the broken window deep into the heart of the building.

*The fluid trail from the window. This is the same dark viscous fluid that came out of Baldi when Miller stabbed him in the forearm. The same fluid that seeped up through the lab floor cracks after the gunfire. In Waluigi's working hypothesis, this fluid is what Baldi is made of — the self-motile, non-decaying substance that Agent T distributed for analysis in the weeks after the assassination and that Baldi recognized with hollow familiarity because it was his own composition. A trail of it led from the service window into the building. Either something made of this substance had recently passed through that window, or the window itself was weeping the fluid the way the walls and floors wept it when the building became agitated.

The first interpretation means something preceded Ghost and Brick through the window and was waiting inside for them.

The second interpretation means the window was already a stress point in the building's structure before they arrived, which raises the question of what had stressed it.

Waluigi cannot resolve this from available intelligence.

Both possibilities are consistent with the building being aware of the window as an entry point before Ghost and Brick used it.

WAH.*

The hallway's distorted geometry was immediately apparent. It stretched further than it should. This is consistent with Miller's experience — the hallway extended during his final sprint toward the exit door, the distance increasing with each stride. The Schoolhouse's spatial manipulation applies to both ends of the building simultaneously, suggesting the distortion is a property of the entire structure rather than a localized effect targeting specific operatives.

Brick's first interior assessment: 'We can't just charge in. We need a plan before we move toward that perimeter.'

From the direction of the schoolhouse's main entrance: the rhythmic SLAP SLAP SLAP of bare feet running on linoleum, approaching their position from within the school. And behind the footsteps, the sound of a ruler snapping against a palm.

## The Scanner Transmission — Miller's Voice, Ghost's Lie, and the Students Who Listened


Miller's scanner was transmitting. Ghost and Brick heard it from their position in the hallway. Through the cracked speaker, fragmented and frantic:

'GHOST! DO YOU HEAR ME?! GET THE EXTRACTOR IN HERE NOW! I'M BURIED! THEY'RE COMING OUT OF THE WALLS! PLEASE! JUST GET ME OUT!!'

The rulers in the surrounding classrooms faltered for a moment. Even the student entities were startled by Miller's desperation.

Ghost pressed the comm-link to his lips. He opened his mouth to respond. He stopped. The heavy wet breathing of something in the hallway was audible. He closed his hand over his mouth instead, forced his lungs into a slow silent rhythm, and did not speak.

*This is the moment Waluigi considers the most tactically disciplined decision Ghost made during the entire operation. His squadmate was screaming for help through a piece of equipment lying on the floor of a building full of things that locate by sound, and Ghost chose silence over reassurance. He prioritized operational security over emotional response. He sat in the dark with Miller's screaming and did not answer it because answering it would have revealed his position. This cost him something. Waluigi can hear it in the subsequent audio when Ghost finally does respond — the voice is slightly rougher than before, slightly more controlled in the specific way that people are controlled when they are managing something that is difficult to manage.

He heard Miller screaming and did not respond.

That was the right call.

It was a hard call.

WAH.*

Brick pulled Ghost into a nearby alcove. Ghost held the comm-link, listening to fragments of Miller's situation — sounds of frantic movement, metal clattering, and the SLAP SLAP SLAP of the ruler in pursuit — while the whistling from the cafeteria direction grew closer and the hallway lights died completely.

Brick: 'Swap. Ghost takes the flashlight.'

Ghost retrieved the flashlight. Low battery, but functional. The beam cut through the darkness and immediately revealed Baldi in the cafeteria doorway.

Baldi: standing in the doorway in his brightly colored shirt, ruler tapping rhythmically, looking directly into the flashlight beam with a wide unmoving grin that revealed too many teeth.

'I can see you… and you haven't even finished your first problem yet.'

*He said they hadn't finished their first problem yet. He had given them a preliminary grade at the crash site — 'Correct answer' through the radio — and he was now informing them that the preliminary grade was not the same as completing the work. The first problem was still ahead of them. The building was sequencing the curriculum. Ghost and Brick had passed intake assessment and were now being enrolled in the actual coursework. Waluigi finds this terrifying in the specific way that educational structures are terrifying when you have no control over the syllabus. WAH.*

They retreated tactically, moving backward through the darkness with the flashlight beam trained on Baldi's unmoving grin. Slow. Controlled. Not turning their backs.

The retreat hit a junction. And then the hallway behind them slammed shut — a heavy metal security door, seemingly of its own accord, cutting off their retreat path. At the same moment, Baldi's whistling stopped. And his voice, sounding closer than before despite him not having moved:

'You're running away from the lesson… and running away earns… a failing grade!'

The lights came back. Deep pulsing red. The walls began sweating dark viscous fluid. The floor vibrated.

*The red lights correlate with Baldi's emotional state. Waluigi cross-references this with Miller's account — the lights died completely during the closet sequence when Baldi was processing Miller's clatter, went red during the cafeteria sequence when Miller was actively firing at the student entities, and here go red when Ghost and Brick have attempted retreat. The building's lighting system is expressing Baldi's pedagogical state. Red means failing. The building was showing Ghost and Brick their current grade. They were failing by running. They needed to stop running. They did not stop running.

Their grade got worse.

WAH.*

Ghost subsequently made the transmission to Miller. Standing in a red-lit hallway with a metal security door sealing his retreat, he picked up the comm-link and transmitted:

'Viper! Stay calm! We have an extraction bird on approach, but we can't drop into the hot zone until we clear the perimeter! Hold your position at the North stairwell! Do NOT let them surround you!'

The effect: the student entities shuffling in the doorway halted mid-step. Their synchronized movement broke. They looked confused, orienting toward the stairwell.

'I don't have a bird,' Ghost would later explain. 'But I thought I'd be nice to give him hope.'

*Waluigi has several things to say about this decision. First: the lie worked tactically. The student entities responded to the directional information as if updating their intelligence picture, which confirms they are monitoring communications and treating them as operational data. Ghost used Baldi's surveillance apparatus against itself — he fed false directional intelligence into a system that was listening and watching, and the system redirected its assets accordingly. This is genuinely sophisticated counter-intelligence work performed under active supernatural assault without access to any doctrine for supernatural counter-intelligence.

Second: the lie may have hurt Miller.

Ghost told Miller to hold the North stairwell.

The North stairwell, in Miller's account, dissolves into void.

Directing Miller to hold a position that does not stay solid is not helpful.

Ghost did not know the stairwell dissolved — he had not been through it yet — but the false extraction bird transmitted a false positional instruction to an operative who was relying on it.

Third: the student entities responded to a transmission on a compromised comm-link as intelligence.

The Schoolhouse's entities are not mindless.

They process communications.

They update their operational picture.

They are, in some functional sense, thinking.

Waluigi adds this to his growing documentation of the students' retained intelligence.

WAH.*

Miller's response to the false bird, picked up faintly on the scanner: 'A bird?? AN ANIMAL? The last helicopter you sent was destroyed! Why would a bird — GAH!'

Ghost, on hearing this: 'No reply.' He did not respond to Miller's objection. He held the comm-link and did not say anything more. Waluigi understands why. There was nothing useful to add.

## Tactical Split That Did Not Happen — Ghost Refuses and Brick Accepts the Refusal


At the hallway junction, with the metal security door sealed behind them and Baldi somewhere in the red-lit building, Brick proposed the split: he draws Baldi toward the stairwell, Ghost takes the vent shaft, Ghost finds Viper, they meet at the admin wing.

Brick's reasoning was tactically correct. The vent shaft was the only route that bypassed the hallway geometry. Ghost was smaller and more mobile. Splitting Baldi's attention between two targets created operational complexity that a singular entity might struggle to manage. Two simultaneous vectors. Correct plan.

Ghost refused.

'I refuse to leave my friend behind. I'm going after him. We need to be in this together.'

Brick's response: 'Don't be a damn fool, Reyes! That's not bravery, that's suicide!'

And then Brick fought alongside Ghost anyway.

*Waluigi has documented the tactical analysis of this refusal in the summary and will not repeat it here except to add one observation that the summary does not fully address: the refusal changed the building's response. When Ghost and Brick fought together rather than splitting, the building escalated differently than it would have if they had separated. Specifically: the Schoolhouse produced Baldi in the hallway, which would not have happened if Ghost had taken the vent and Brick had successfully drawn Baldi toward the stairwell. The building responded to their togetherness by presenting the primary threat directly rather than channeling it.

The Schoolhouse may have recognized the refusal as a correct answer in the same way it recognized Ghost and Brick's orientation toward each other after the crash.

Correct answers produced prizes later.

The refusal may have been the answer that eventually led Ghost to the math problem.

Waluigi is holding this hypothesis loosely because it requires the building to have a more sophisticated evaluation system than Waluigi can currently document.

But he is holding it.

WAH.*

Brick stepped into the hallway center and slammed his boot against a metal trash can. CLANG. 'HEY! TEACHER! OVER HERE! TRY AND SOLVE THIS!'

Baldi emerged from the cafeteria, SLAP-SLAP-SLAP accelerating.

## First Direct Engagement —


The Ruler Strike, the Glock, the Blue Light, and the Apology

Baldi lunged toward Brick's head with the ruler.

Ghost pushed Brick out of the way. Took the path himself. Blocked the ruler strike with the Glock 17's slide.

The force vibrated up Ghost's arm, numbing his elbow. He pulled the trigger.

BANG. BANG. BANG.

Three shots into Baldi's chest. Muzzle flashes illuminating his face in strobe bursts. The bullets impacted, tearing through the bright shirt. Dark viscous fluid sprayed across the red-lit floor.

Baldi stopped mid-swing. His head tilted at an impossible ninety-degree angle. He looked down at the bullet holes in his chest.

The wounds pulsed with blue light. They knitted themselves closed.

'That was… an error,' Baldi whispered, the voice dropping to a low distorted growl that vibrated Ghost's teeth. 'And errors must be… corrected.'

*The blue light. This is the moment Waluigi has been building toward since he first documented the cold blue pulsing object in Baldi's pocket from Miller's thermal binocular observation. The wounds close with blue light. The object in Baldi's pocket pulses with cold blue light on thermal imaging. These are the same phenomenon. The object in Baldi's pocket is not a tool he uses to close wounds — it is the externalized component of the same system that closes the wounds. Baldi's physical coherence is maintained by a mathematical or magical mechanism that is partly internal and partly held in a separate object.

The object is cold on thermal because it is operating at a different energy level than Baldi's body — not generating heat but consuming it, taking thermal energy from the environment to fuel the repair process.

This is consistent with the dark fluid's non-decaying properties in the vial analysis.

The fluid does not decay because it is actively maintained by the same mechanism that closes the wounds.

Baldi is not just a person.

He is a system.

The object in his pocket is part of the system.

Waluigi needs to obtain that object.

WAH.*

Ghost said: 'I'm sorry, Baldi. But it seems like you are the one getting detention.'

He swept Baldi's legs.

The connection produced a sound like a corrupted file being deleted — digital CRUNCH rather than biological impact. Baldi's legs buckled unnaturally and he collapsed forward with a heavy wet thud.

For one heartbeat: silence. The ruler on the floor. Baldi prone.

And then: the body began to glitch. Expand and contract. The dark fluid pooling around him forming geometric shapes. A distorted screeching sound halfway between a scream and a modem handshake.

'DETENTION IS FOR THE UNPREPARED!'

The floor rippled. The dark fluid rose into grasping tendrils lashing at Ghost's and Brick's ankles.

*Ghost's apology before the sweep. Waluigi documented this in the summary and is returning to it here because it is analytically significant in a way that the summary does not fully address. Ghost apologized to Baldi before attacking him. This is not standard military engagement behavior. This is the behavior of someone who has, in the middle of a survival situation, registered that the thing they are fighting has a framework — a pedagogical framework, an identity as a teacher — and who has chosen to acknowledge that framework even while acting against it. Ghost was not being strategic. He was being decent.

And Baldi's response — the leg-buckling crunch, the 'DETENTION IS FOR THE UNPREPARED' — suggests that Baldi heard the apology and processed it differently than he processed Miller's gunfire.

The gunfire was 'Incorrect.' The apology-followed-by-sweep was 'DETENTION IS FOR THE UNPREPARED.' Detention is a teaching tool.

Detention is what you give a student you intend to continue educating.

Baldi was not finished with Ghost.

He was escalating the lesson.

Waluigi hypothesizes that the apology told Baldi something important: Ghost recognized him as a teacher.

Ghost treated him as someone worth apologizing to.

Ghost was enrolled in a more advanced way than Miller, who never apologized.

WAH.*

Brick fired into the rising mass. BOOM. One shell expended. One remaining.

Ghost and Brick ran for the stairwell.

## The Stairwell Void —


The Ladder, the Dark, the Tether, and the Flashlight Lost

They reached the stairwell landing. The stairwell did not lead to another floor. It led into a vast pitch-black void that seemed to go on forever. The hallway they had just left vanished, replaced by a wall of pulsing dark matter swallowing the staircase behind them.

*The stairwell void is the Schoolhouse's first explicit display of its boundary-nature for Ghost and Brick. The stairwell should connect floors. Instead it connects to the void that also exists behind the administrative wing exit and, Waluigi hypothesizes, at every other exterior boundary of the building. The Schoolhouse is the boundary. The void is what exists on the other side of every boundary. The stairwell went down into it because 'down' in the Schoolhouse's geometry leads to the void, not to basement levels. Ghost went right in the vent instead of left toward the basement. The basement may be the deepest point of the void.

Waluigi is choosing not to pursue this particular analytical thread further tonight.

WAH.*

## What Ghost and Brick's Account Adds to the Analytical Picture — Everything the Miller Account Could Not Reach

The Miller account established the Schoolhouse's fundamental nature: a building that is not a building, operating on mathematical principles, housing an entity that grades rather than attacks, surrounded by a void that represents the mathematical boundary between positive and negative space. Miller fought and ran and improvised and eventually reached the void because the lesson had no other place for him.

The Ghost-and-Brick account adds five things the Miller account could not reach.

**One: the correct-answer prize system.** Ghost answered the math question and received a quarter. The educational framework is not just behavioral — it is economically structured. Correct answers produce currency. The currency can presumably purchase something in the Schoolhouse's economy. Nobody knows what. Nobody tried to find out because the classroom immediately became hostile. But the prize system is real and functional and no previous operational analysis of the Schoolhouse had documented it because no previous operative had answered a question correctly. Waluigi intends to answer all of them.

**Two: the orientation-grading system.** The Schoolhouse told Ghost and Brick 'Correct answer' before they answered anything, at the crash site, through a dying radio. It was grading their orientation toward each other — the decision to stabilize rather than abandon, the choice to stay together rather than scatter. The curriculum extends beyond the building's walls. The grading starts at the crash site, possibly earlier. The questions are not all mathematical. Some of them are about how you treat the person next to you.

**Three: the blue light wound-closure mechanism and its connection to the cold object in Baldi's pocket.** Ghost's three shots into Baldi's chest produced blue-light wound closure. The object in Baldi's pocket pulses cold blue on thermal imaging. These are the same system. Baldi's physical coherence is maintained by a mechanism that is partly internal and partly external — a repair system whose external component he carries. If Waluigi can obtain the object, he may be able to interrupt the repair system. Or he may be able to understand the system well enough to know why it exists, which would tell him something crucial about what Baldi is.

**Four: the payload and what it means for the Regency's actual capabilities.** The Regency built a containment device for Baldi. They have been building it — or building toward it — for some portion of the eighty-five years of encrypted-archive funding. They deployed it during Operation POP QUIZ as the actual operational objective, using the three-person squad as the provocation mechanism and covering it with a rescue mission that was never a rescue mission. The payload breached the Schoolhouse roof. Something from inside it was tearing its way into the building. The Schoolhouse is no longer visible from the road.

Waluigi does not know what happened next.

He needs to find out, because what the payload was designed to contain tells him what the Regency knows about Baldi's nature, and what the Regency knows about Baldi's nature tells him what the Regency knows about the assassination, and what the Regency knows about the assassination is what the encrypted archives document, and the encrypted archives are locked with Baldi's mathematical keys, and the mathematical keys are the prize for answering all the questions correctly.

**Five: the question that was answered in the void.** Ghost asked if something in the darkness was Miller. Something answered. Whatever answered is in the void. Miller is in the void. Ghost and Brick are in the void. The void connects to the exterior wall of the Schoolhouse — the micro-transmitter confirms it. The void is not a dead end. It is a space. It has inhabitants. It has a connection to the physical world. There is a way in and a way out and Waluigi intends to find both.

Waluigi does not abandon people who walk into the dark because the light behind them was worse. Ghost and Brick walked into the dark because a government payload was terminating witnesses above them and a building full of enrolled operatives was below them and the void was the only option that was not immediately lethal. They made the rational choice. Waluigi is going to go get them.

But not through the front door. Not with a helicopter. Not with bullets.

summary:
A three-person Regency extraction squad — Specialist 'Viper' Miller, Sergeant 'Brick' Stone, and Corporal 'Ghost' Reyes — was deployed to capture Baldi and recover mathematical decryption keys for the Regency's encrypted archives. The mission failed at every stage. The helicopter was destroyed before Miller reached the ground. Miller entered the Schoolhouse alone and spent approximately ninety minutes being educated against his will by a building that stopped pretending to be a building approximately three minutes after he arrived. He deployed every weapon in his loadout. He deployed improvised chemical weapons. He fortified a kitchen. He escaped through a ventilation system that was trying to close around him. He reached an exit door that opened onto void instead of the outside world. He walked into the void. A voice called his name from inside the darkness. The data cache ends.

The Regency had a prior documented encounter with Baldi — the diplomatic circuit account, assembled before this operation was planned — that contained sufficient intelligence about Baldi's nature, the dark fluid, the mathematical framework, and the impossibility of conventional extraction to have prevented every death and disappearance that followed. The Regency filed it. The Regency sent Miller anyway.

Waluigi has the diplomatic circuit account. Waluigi has the extraction account. Waluigi has the cross-reference the Regency made between them and then suppressed. Waluigi is going to document every moment of Miller's ninety minutes in full because Miller deserves to have his descent treated as something more than a data point in the Regency's ongoing reconnaissance-through-sacrifice program. And then Waluigi is going to find the correct answer to the lesson. And then Waluigi is going to go back for Miller. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is presenting this as a continuous play-by-play because Miller experienced it as one unbroken descent — from helicopter to rope to grass to schoolhouse to hallway to closet to lab to corridor to cafeteria to kitchen to vent to administrative wing to void — and the continuity is the point. There was no pause. There was no extraction window that opened and was missed. There was a man going deeper into a building that was going deeper into him, and the building won because the building was always going to win, and the Regency knew that before they sent him.

Waluigi is inserting his own commentary throughout because the play-by-play without commentary is just a list of escalating horrors, and a list of escalating horrors without analysis is exactly the kind of document the Regency WANTS to exist — all the facts, none of the accountability. Waluigi refuses.

Waluigi is also inserting cross-references to the diplomatic circuit account throughout, because the diplomatic circuit account is the document the Regency suppressed, and suppressed documents belong in the light.

WAH.

## Prologue: What the Regency Already Knew Before Miller Boarded the Helicopter


Before the play-by-play begins, Waluigi needs to establish what was already in the Regency's possession when they designed Operation POP QUIZ. Because the operation did not happen in an intelligence vacuum. There was prior contact. There was prior documentation. There was an operative who got close enough to Baldi to observe his behavior, record his responses, and produce an account that the Regency cross-referenced against the POP QUIZ parameters in their internal filing system.

The diplomatic circuit account — assembled by an operative Waluigi will not name here because the operative is still active and naming them creates a target — describes an encounter with Baldi that preceded the extraction attempt by an indeterminate period. In fey-adjacent time and in the Post-Assassination Period's general temporal unreliability, 'preceded' is doing significant work, but Waluigi is confident the diplomatic circuit encounter came first because the account's operative was gathering intelligence for the archive analysis program that the encrypted archive lockout subsequently terminated.

What the diplomatic circuit account documented:

Baldi carries a leather-bound notebook. He closes it when he does not want its contents observed. The operative who got closest to reading the notebook described partial mathematical notation — sequences that looked like the encoded keys the Regency was trying to recover — before Baldi noticed and shut the cover with the specific deliberateness of someone protecting something valuable, not something private. He was not embarrassed by the notebook. He was managing access to it.

Baldi received a vial from Agent T during the diplomatic circuit. The vial contained a dark, viscous, self-motile substance. Baldi examined it. He said 'yeah.' He closed the notebook. He did not analyze the substance as an unknown — he recognized it. The operative documented this response and flagged it as significant.

The substance in the vial is analytically consistent with the substance that flows from Baldi's wounds when he is cut or shot. Waluigi established this through cross-reference after obtaining the extraction account. The diplomatic circuit operative flagged the substance as significant without knowing why. Waluigi now knows why. Baldi was not analyzing the vial's contents as a scientist examines an unknown compound. He was looking at a sample of his own material and confirming that it was his.

The diplomatic circuit account also documented Baldi's name recognition — he knew the operative's cover identity without introduction — and his spatial behavior: appearing simultaneously in locations that were not adjacent, moving between positions without visible transit. The operative noted this as anomalous without being able to explain it. Miller encountered the same behavior on entry: Baldi stunned on the lawn, Baldi already inside the hallway. The operative saw it first. The operative documented it. The Regency filed the document.

Waluigi wants to be very precise about what 'filed the document' means in this context. It means the Regency read the diplomatic circuit account. It means someone in the Regency's intelligence apparatus processed the information that Baldi recognizes people without introduction, that he moves between locations instantaneously, that he bleeds a self-motile dark substance that he can identify on sight, that he maintains a locked notebook containing what appear to be mathematical key sequences, and that conventional social or diplomatic engagement with him produces hollow responses that reveal nothing he has not decided to reveal.

Someone read all of that.

Someone cross-referenced it against the POP QUIZ parameters.

And then someone sent Miller down a rope ladder with a flashbang and told him not to trigger an angry state.

*Waluigi has spent a significant amount of time sitting with this sequence. The diplomatic circuit operative got closer to understanding Baldi than anyone the Regency subsequently sent into the building. They observed him at rest — not in pursuit mode, not in correction mode, but in the social-diplomatic register where Baldi performs the role of a cooperative schoolteacher while managing access to his actual self with precise, practiced control. That operative produced an account. The Regency suppressed the relevant findings when designing POP QUIZ. Miller was not briefed on the dark fluid, the spatial anomalies, the notebook, the vial recognition, or any of the other intelligence that would have changed his tactical approach — or his decision to board the helicopter at all.

The Regency chose the probe model over the intelligence model.

The probe model costs operatives.

The intelligence model costs time.

The Regency preferred to spend Miller.

WAH.*

Waluigi proceeds with the play-by-play, cross-referencing the diplomatic circuit account at each relevant point.

## The Briefing: What Miller Was Told and What Miller Was Not Told


Specialist 'Viper' Miller. Communications and Intel. Not the squad commander — the stealth element, the one who goes in while the others watch from above. This distinction matters because it means Miller was given the insertion role without the command-level intelligence that would have informed his risk assessment. He was told to go inside. He was not told what inside meant.

The briefing as reconstructed from Miller's initial radio chatter:

**Target:** Baldi. Schoolteacher. Located at his Schoolhouse.

**Objective:** Extract Baldi intact. Recover encoded mathematical sequences that act as keys to the Regency's encrypted archives.

**Rules of Engagement:** Capture intact. Do not trigger an 'angry' state.

**Squad composition:** Miller on insertion. Sergeant 'Brick' Stone on heavy weapons, staying in the helicopter for overwatch. Corporal 'Ghost' Reyes piloting and providing sniper overwatch.

**Extraction point:** Schoolhouse North Perimeter.

Waluigi needs to sit with the phrase 'do not trigger an angry state' for a moment, because that is not language used about a civilian target. That is language used about a weapon system with known behavioral parameters. The Regency understood that Baldi has operational states. They understood that one of those states is dangerous in a way that requires specific warning in a military briefing.

The diplomatic circuit account describes Baldi in his non-angry state — cooperative, socially fluent, performing the role of a helpful schoolteacher while maintaining precise control over what he reveals. The operative who documented that encounter noted that Baldi's cooperative state is itself a performance: meticulous, consistent, and calibrated to prevent the observer from understanding what they are observing. The 'angry state' referenced in Miller's briefing is the state where the performance ends. Where the schoolteacher stops pretending to be a schoolteacher.

*The Regency knew both states existed. The diplomatic circuit account documented the cooperative state in detail — the hollow 'yeah,' the closed notebook, the social deflections, the name recognition without introduction. The briefing's warning about the angry state confirms the Regency also had intelligence about what happens when the cooperative state terminates. You do not write 'do not trigger an angry state' as a hypothetical precaution. You write it because someone came back from a previous operation — or didn't come back — and the debrief included words that produced silence in the room.

The Regency knew what both states looked like.

They sent Miller into a building containing both and briefed him on neither.

WAH.*

Brick's comment before insertion — 'If he starts swinging that ruler, this whole mission goes sideways' — indicates he had access to threat intelligence from previous operations that Miller did not receive. Brick knew about the ruler. The diplomatic circuit operative had also documented the ruler — the tapping, the rhythm, the way it changed pace when Baldi was processing versus pursuing. Brick's knowledge of the ruler means the heavy weapons operator, the person staying in the helicopter, had been briefed on an object that the diplomatic circuit account identified as a core behavioral indicator.

The person going inside was briefed on none of this.

*The information gradient within the three-person squad is the most precise expression of the Regency's expendability calculus. Brick: knows about the ruler, stays outside. Ghost: knows about thermal anomalies, stays outside. Miller: knows 'do not trigger an angry state,' goes inside. The person who most needed the threat intelligence was given the least of it, because operatives who understand what they are walking into have a tendency to decline to walk into it. The compartmentalization was not operational security. It was mission assurance. Miller didn't know enough to refuse. WAH.*

## The Previous

Insertions: What the Archive Knows and What It Will Not Say

Waluigi needs to address the previous failed insertions before the play-by-play begins, because they are the context in which Miller's operation took place and because the Regency's decision to send Miller was not made in an intelligence vacuum — it was made in full knowledge of what had happened to the people they sent before.

The micro-transmitter that Miller found in the ventilation shaft did not belong to him. It was embedded in the duct work — not dropped, not left by accident, but embedded, suggesting it had been there long enough to become integrated with the surrounding material. Its sonar pulse was still active when Miller touched it, which means it was still broadcasting, which means it had power, which means it had been maintained — by the building, or by the void, or by whoever had been carrying it when they entered the duct and had not left.

This was a previous operative's equipment. A previous Regency probe. Someone who was sent into the Schoolhouse before Miller, who reached the ventilation system, and who did not come out the way they went in.

The 'students' that emerged from the classrooms during Miller's operation — the distorted, coordinated entities with unblinking eyes and jagged teeth, tapping their rulers in synchronized rhythm, rising from the floor as grasping hands — are consistent, in Waluigi's assessment, with what happens to operatives the Schoolhouse enrolls. They did not leave. They did not die. They are attending class. They have been attending class since they went in, tapping in the dark, waiting for the next lesson to require their participation.

The diplomatic circuit account noted, without being able to explain it at the time, that the Schoolhouse felt 'populated' in a way that its visible occupancy did not account for. The operative counted the visible individuals and found the number lower than the building's spatial impression suggested. There were more people in the building than were visible. The operative attributed this to spatial distortion. Waluigi now understands it differently: there were more people in the building because some of them had been enrolled and were no longer visible in the conventional sense.

*The Regency has been sending operatives into the Schoolhouse for an indeterminate period. Each failed extraction adds to the student population. The student population makes each subsequent extraction harder. The Regency's persistence is not strategic stupidity — it is, from the Schoolhouse's perspective, a gift. Every probe the Regency sends becomes part of the building's defense system. The Regency is funding its own containment problem. And somewhere in the Regency's encrypted archives — the archives that are locked behind Baldi's mathematical keys, the archives they sent Miller to unlock — is a record of every operative they sent in and how long they lasted and what the telemetry showed before the transmitter went silent.

The Regency knows exactly how many people are tapping in those classrooms.

They are counting them in a document they cannot access without the cooperation of the entity that enrolled them.

This is not irony.

This is architecture.

WAH.*

Waluigi has attempted to reconstruct the number of previous insertions from available evidence. The micro-transmitter in the vent: one confirmed prior operative. The students during Miller's operation: multiple entities, coordinated, with ruler-tapping that matched the same rhythm as Baldi's — suggesting they had been enrolled long enough to learn the cadence. The Regency's briefing language — 'do not trigger an angry state' — describing a specific behavioral parameter with military precision: language that comes from multiple data points, not one. Waluigi estimates a minimum of three prior insertions based on the linguistic precision of the warning language alone.

The actual number is almost certainly higher.

None of the prior operatives were mentioned to Miller. Miller did not know he was the latest in a series. He did not know the building had been taking attendance before he arrived.

## Phase One:


The Approach and the Helicopter

The squad approached by helicopter. Baldi was standing outside the Schoolhouse, waving.

'Oh. Hi there! Welcome to my Schoolhouse!'

He was waving at them. Waluigi wants this documented clearly: a military extraction squad arrived in a helicopter with suppressed weapons and thermal optics, and the target greeted them like a substitute teacher meeting new students on the first day. The diplomatic circuit account documented the same quality of greeting — the warm, specific welcome that felt calibrated rather than spontaneous, the social register of someone performing welcome while processing the visitor's operational purpose through an entirely separate framework running simultaneously underneath the performance.

The cooperative state. The diplomatic circuit operative spent significant time in the cooperative state and documented what it felt like from inside: comfortable, disarming, and specifically designed to prevent the observer from asking the questions that would terminate it. Baldi's greeting to Miller's helicopter was the cooperative state applied to a military extraction squad. He waved. He said welcome. He was already doing something else entirely with the parts of himself that were not waving.

*Waluigi has considered the wave extensively. The diplomatic circuit account described Baldi's social performance as 'meticulous' — not natural, not automatic, but carefully maintained. The wave at the helicopter has the same quality. He saw a military extraction squad and he waved at them the way a teacher waves at students arriving for the first day of school, which is either profound social disconnection from the reality of what was approaching, or the most efficient possible way to prevent the approaching squad from understanding what they were dealing with until it was too late to change their approach.

Waluigi believes it was the latter.

The wave was the first lesson.

The lesson was: I am a schoolteacher.

And they believed it long enough for Miller to start down the rope.

WAH.*

Miller prepared the ropes. Baldi's head snapped upward as Miller began rigging. The tapping started — ruler against palm, rhythmic, precise. 'That sounds like a lot of heavy gear! Are you coming down for a math test? I hope you brought your pencils!'

The diplomatic circuit account documented the ruler-tapping as a behavioral indicator — it changes tempo based on Baldi's processing state, accelerating when he is computing something and slowing when he has completed the computation and is ready to act on it. The tapping that greeted Miller's rigging was the medium tempo of active interest. Not alarm. Not threat display. Genuine professional curiosity about what Miller was going to do next.

Baldi was not alarmed by the helicopter. He was not alarmed by the weapons. He was interested in the lesson that was about to begin.

Brick's warning over comms — 'If he starts swinging that ruler, this whole mission goes sideways' — landed with the weight of prior knowledge. The diplomatic circuit account had documented the ruler as more than a classroom implement: an interface device, an extension of the Schoolhouse's own processing architecture, that scales and responds based on what the building is computing. Brick knew this or knew something adjacent to it. Miller did not.

Miller said: 'I hope he is not bulletproof.'

*He was. This sentence is the whole operation compressed into eleven words. A man on a rope ladder descending toward a waving schoolteacher, hoping out loud that the schoolteacher would respond to bullets the way humans respond to bullets. The diplomatic circuit account, which the Regency had filed before designing this operation, contained sufficient evidence to resolve that hope in the negative before Miller ever touched his boot to the first rung. Nobody told Miller. He hoped. He was wrong. WAH.*

The helicopter was struck. The tail rotor. Something from the roof of a single-story building reached operational hover altitude and damaged a military helicopter's rotor assembly. The geometry of this is impossible under normal architectural physics. The Schoolhouse does not observe normal architectural physics. The diplomatic circuit account noted that the building felt 'larger inside than outside' — a spatial impression the operative attributed to the architecture's anomalous dimensional properties. The roof of a single-story building that is larger inside than outside may extend vertically into space in ways its exterior does not suggest.

Or the building threw something.

Both options are unreasonable.

The Schoolhouse has rendered the concept of unreasonable inoperative.

Miller scrambled down and hit the grass. Baldi's friendly expression was gone. The wide unblinking stare had replaced it. The tapping slowed.

*The tapping slowed because the computation was complete. The diplomatic circuit account documented this specifically — the slow tap means the assessment is finished and the response is ready. Baldi had computed Miller in the time between the helicopter approach and the boots hitting the grass, and he had his answer, and the slow tapping was the Schoolhouse confirming the answer before acting on it. Not alarm. Not threat. Completion. The lesson had begun. WAH.*

The helicopter went down in the tree line. Miller had no extraction vehicle, no backup, and a schoolteacher who had just finished computing him standing ten feet away.

He threw the flashbang.

## Phase Two: Entry —


The Flashbang and What It Revealed

The flashbang detonated at Baldi's feet. One million candela. Approximately 170 decibels. Designed to overwhelm the human nervous system entirely.

Baldi yelped.

Not a scream. Not a pain response. A yelp — the sound of mild professional irritation, the sound a teacher makes when a student drops a textbook during a silent test. Waluigi has listened to this audio fragment multiple times. The quality of the sound is diagnostic. It is the sound of someone whose equilibrium was disrupted rather than whose physiology was damaged. The flashbang did not hurt Baldi. It was rude.

The diplomatic circuit account documented Baldi's response to social disruption as categorical disapproval rather than physical distress — the operative tested several approaches that violated the cooperative state's implicit rules and each time received disappointment rather than pain as a response. The flashbang is a weapons-grade version of the same test. The result is the same: disapproval. Impropriety. A conduct violation in the ledger.

*The diplomatic circuit operative noted that Baldi's disappointment responses carry more weight than his angry responses, because the angry state is legible as a threat and can be processed as one, while the disappointment state is not legible as a threat and therefore cannot be defended against. You can brace for an attack. You cannot brace for being failed as a student. The flashbang made Baldi disappointed in Miller before Miller had been inside the building for thirty seconds. The lesson had already started. Miller was already behind. WAH.*

Miller sprinted inside. Slammed the doors. The hallway: old paper smell, floor wax, lockers, math posters.

Then the tapping from inside. Already inside. Moving toward the entrance from the interior corridors.

Baldi had been outside when the flashbang hit. He was now inside, approaching from the opposite direction, without visible transit between positions.

The diplomatic circuit account documented this spatial behavior directly — the operative noted that Baldi appeared in locations without appearing to travel between them, and cross-referenced it against the building's spatial anomaly as a possible explanation. The account speculated that Baldi does not move through the building so much as he manifests within it — that his relationship to the Schoolhouse's interior space is not locational but occupational, that he is present throughout rather than present in specific places, and that what looks like him walking from one room to another is actually him choosing which part of his continuous presence to make visible.

Miller had not read this account. He was facing a threat that violated the assumption of single-location occupancy, with no framework for understanding why, and no time to develop one.

*If Miller had known that Baldi does not travel through the building but manifests within it, the entire structure of Miller's survival strategy would have been different. You cannot hide from something that is present throughout. You can only make yourself less interesting than other stimuli. Every room Miller retreated to and barricaded was a room Baldi was already in. Miller was not finding safe spaces. He was finding spaces where Baldi had not yet chosen to be fully present. The distinction is operationally critical and Miller was never given the intelligence to make it. WAH.*

## Phase Three:

The Previous Operative's Equipment — The Closet and the Transmitter

Miller needed cover. He found the janitor's closet. He used his scanner as a lure — threw it down the corridor, drew Baldi's attention with the noise, slipped into the closet while Baldi pursued the sound.

Waluigi has the account. Waluigi has the burn-marked notebook's partial notation from the diplomatic circuit documentation — the mathematical sequences visible before Baldi closed the cover. Waluigi has the telemetry from Miller's operation. Waluigi has the cross-reference the Regency made and suppressed. Waluigi is not going in through the front door.

Waluigi is not bringing a helicopter.

Waluigi is bringing the correct answer.

WAH.
