summary: Leo, Luigi, and Professor E. Gadd are three days out from the Clockwork Spire on a Mages' Guild transport that did not include dinner. The first night produced, in order: a spectral entity of significant mass testing the roof of the Research and Logistics Car, Leo deploying the Prototype-X Poltergust in Hyper-Suction Mode without reading the manual, a structural breach in the ceiling, a localized depressurization event, an improvised spectral catapult using the Poltergust's outtake valve, the entity being launched into the tunnel at high velocity, emergency tarp application with green sealant, an unscheduled stop at the abandoned Blackwood Junction, the discovery that the passenger carriages appear empty, a hypothesis from Leo that the party may be in a localized dimensional pocket rather than the passengers having disappeared, the identification of a light-consuming void near a luggage rack, and Professor E. Gadd handing Leo the Ionic Disruptor-Z prototype, which Leo then handed to Luigi, which Luigi is currently holding with the specific body language of a man who has been handed a live grenade and told it is his responsibility now. Leo has just said something to Luigi that the train's ambient noise nearly swallowed. Waluigi is documenting this from secondhand sources and finds the entire sequence deeply characteristic of how operations go when the Mages' Guild is involved in the logistics.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the first night aboard the Maglev Express because it contains several things that deserve full archival attention: an improvised spectral catapult that E. Gadd has described as 'a feat of accidental engineering that defies every law of physics I know,' a dimensional pocket hypothesis that Leo arrived at through observation rather than scientific training, and a moment between Leo and Luigi that happened in a dark train carriage with a pulsating void nearby and that Waluigi suspects will matter more than the void does in the long run.

Waluigi wants to note the logistical context before documenting the events themselves, because the logistical context is its own kind of commentary. The Mages' Guild arranged this transport. The Guild is an institution that maintains the Anti-Virus Citadel, operates through the ISP Toll-Bridge's regulatory frameworks, and has enough institutional reach to send a senior researcher, a field operative, and a ghost hunter on a classified mission to a haunted manor. The Guild did not arrange dinner. The Guild did not arrange a train with functioning passenger services. The Guild provided a Research and Logistics Car, a route schematic with a skull-and-crossbones symbol marking the subterranean trench section, and a mission that requires three days of transit through territory with documented spectral activity.

No dinner.

Waluigi finds this emblematic of how the Guild operates: maximum secrecy, minimum hospitality, and a complete absence of the amenities that make dangerous missions survivable by people who are not already dead.

## The Entity on the Roof: 11:42 PM


The sequence began with Leo looking for a dinner menu on the laminated card clipped to the seat's edge, which is either optimism or the specific coping mechanism of someone who has decided that normalcy is worth performing even when the environment has stopped cooperating with it. Luigi's response — pointing out that they were heading toward a haunted manor leaking ectoplasm — indicates that Luigi had already abandoned the normalcy performance and was operating in the register of someone who has accepted the situation and is now purely afraid of it.

Luigi's briefing was accurate and comprehensive. Three days to the Clockwork Spire. Calibration work needed on both Poltergusts for Class-V spectral manifestations. Blueprint review required because E. Gadd's historical records have blind spots. Sleep recommended because fainting when a ghost screams is tactically inadvisable. The briefing was delivered in a low whisper with one eye on the curtained door, which is the intelligence-sharing posture of someone who has learned that eavesdroppers exist even on classified transports.

Waluigi notes: Luigi's briefing was excellent. Luigi is not incapable. Luigi is afraid, which is different from incapable, and the difference is important because fear is a condition that can be worked with and incapability is a condition that cannot. The rest of the night's events are partially a documentation of that distinction being tested.

The entity arrived via the roof at approximately 11:42 PM by E. Gadd's chronometer. The ecto-meter detected a significant surge in spectral density directly above the Research and Logistics Car. E. Gadd's radar screen showed several jagged pulsing blips around the car's perimeter. His mass displacement analysis suggested the entity was dense, concentrated, not a sprawling cloud but something with physical heft — 'like a much larger version of a Boo, but with much more physical heft.'

The thudding was rhythmic. The scraping was sharp. The carriage lights flickered. A wrench left the table under the vibration.

Leo observed that the Great Crest Tunnel was approaching — and that the tunnel's reduced clearance might interact with an entity large enough to be generating the mass displacement readings E. Gadd was recording. This is the correct tactical observation: the tunnel reduces the entity's operational space. The question of whether the entity was large enough to fit through the tunnel is also the correct follow-up question.

E. Gadd's assessment was that the entity was not mountain-sized but was large enough to exert immense pressure on structural integrity, and that it was hugging the curve of the car. The tunnel entrance was visible through the window. The clawing sound on the roof had become frantic.

## The Hyper-Suction


Incident: The Improvised Catapult

Leo opened the window. Leo flipped the switch for Hyper-Suction Mode. Leo aimed the Prototype-X upward. Leo fired it.

Waluigi wants to document Leo's decision-making process here because it is the decision-making process that will characterize Leo's operational style for the rest of this mission and possibly the rest of this crisis: assessment of available tools, selection of the most direct application, execution before the people around him can articulate all the reasons execution is inadvisable. Luigi said 'the recoil was bad on this right' during the warning attempt. The warning was accurate. The recoil was catastrophic.

The Prototype-X in Hyper-Suction Mode with the Hyper-Suction switch engaged produced a localized vacuum force that pulled at the ceiling with enough force to buckle the metal plating inward. The entity on the roof — the dense, concentrated mass that had been clawing at the car — was caught in the vacuum's pull. The ceiling began to deform.

E. Gadd's assessment during the chaos: 'It's working! Or it's making things worse! I can't tell through all this hullabaloo!'

Waluigi finds E. Gadd's real-time analysis during the Hyper-Suction incident one of the most honest scientific statements in this entire record. It was working and making things worse simultaneously, which is the precise description of every high-stakes improvised intervention: the desired outcome and the unintended consequences are both happening at the same time and it is genuinely impossible to determine which is winning until the dust settles.

The train entered the Great Crest Tunnel. The sudden loss of external light caused the vacuum effect to invert for a split second due to the pressure change. Instead of pulling upward, the Prototype-X produced one final spasmodic hiccup, sucking tunnel-chilled air inward. Leo was thrown sideways. A windowpane shattered. The entity — now partially inside the compartment, dragged through the structural gap created by the ceiling deformation — hit the floorboards with a wet impact.

Leo aimed at it directly. Leo pulled it into override.

The entity was yanked downward through the ceiling breach. The ceiling tore. A dark mass of shadowy translucent limbs was forcibly dragged through the structural gap and hit the floorboards with a shockwave that killed the lights. The car was lit only by the Poltergust's pulsing blue glow.

Leo smiled and aimed directly at the creature.

The Prototype-X began to pulse with erratic blinding rhythm. The entity's form rippled as it was stretched toward the nozzle. The pressure in the room reached a breaking point. A bolt sheared off from the main housing, ricocheted around the room, narrowly missed Luigi's head.

E. Gadd identified the problem: the polarity was reversing. The vacuum wasn't pulling the entity in — it was acting as a localized singularity, compressing the essence rather than capturing it. This was the moment to shut it down.

Leo asked how.

E. Gadd explained the emergency release valve — the small lever with the red insignia near the base of the nozzle — and the requirement to vent the excess ether simultaneously. He warned that venting too much at once would produce a depressurization event that could blow them into the tunnel walls.

Leo did not use the emergency release valve.

Leo aimed the outtake valve at the entity and discharged it.

The discharge hit with cannon-blast force. The recoil knocked Leo backward. The beam of pressurized ether and captured shadow slammed into the compressed entity and propelled it through the ceiling breach and out of the car at a velocity E. Gadd later described as equivalent to a siege engine projectile.

The entity was gone. The car was dark. The Prototype-X was smoking. Luigi was whimpering in a corner. E. Gadd was behind a crate calling it 'a feat of accidental engineering.'

Waluigi notes: Leo turned a Poltergust into a spectral catapult by accident and it worked. This is the specific kind of operational outcome that builds dangerous confidence — the thing that should not have worked worked, and now Leo knows that the thing that should not work sometimes does, which means future situations will be evaluated against the knowledge that improbable solutions sometimes succeed. Waluigi is watching this calibration with attention.

## Blackwood Junction:


The Empty Carriages

The cleanup was collaborative and uneven. E. Gadd contributed green sealant and a handheld adhesive sprayer and frantic scientific commentary. Luigi contributed the heavy canvas tarp and his own body weight in panic. Leo contributed the other end of the tarp and the observation that they needed to be winning rather than almost winning, which Luigi found insufficient comfort but which was operationally correct.

The tarp held. The breach was sealed enough to prevent catastrophic depressurization. The car was not clean. It was not presentable. It was a salvage, not a restoration.

The train stopped at Blackwood Junction.

Blackwood Junction is documented in E. Gadd's route schematic as a derelict waypoint, abandoned by the Regency after the last spectral surge. The station is illuminated by sickly greenish lanterns. The iron pillars are draped in solidified ectoplasm. Rhythmic tapping from the dark corners of the station buildings is not machinery. A shadowy shape detached from a pillar and drifted toward the passing train as they rolled in.

The stop was not scheduled. The stop was not expected. E. Gadd's analysis: the tracks may be blocked, or the command network may be compromised. Luigi's analysis: 'the only friendly faces are probably going to be teeth.'

Leo proposed exploring the rest of the train. This is, again, the direct application of the most obvious available action: they did not know what was happening because they had been confined to one car. The way to learn what was happening was to see more of the train. This is correct.

Luigi agreed under protest, which is Luigi's characteristic form of agreement throughout this entire documented sequence. He agrees to everything eventually. The agreements come wrapped in specific and vivid descriptions of all the ways the thing he is agreeing to might kill him. But he agrees. Waluigi is noting this pattern because it is important: Luigi describes the danger in exhaustive detail and then goes anyway. This is not cowardice. This is a man with a comprehensive and accurate threat assessment who has decided that going anyway is required.

The first passenger carriage was empty. E. Gadd's specter-scope detected ectoplasmic condensation settling on the upholstery like frost. A single child-sized shoe lay abandoned in the aisle, half-submerged in glowing residue.

Leo's hypothesis: the party may not have encountered a massacre or abduction. They may be in a localized dimensional pocket. The evidence: no blood, no disrupted seating, no signs of struggle, no snack wrappers. The emptiness was too clean. Too surgical. If they had slipped into a sub-stratum of reality, the passengers would not have disappeared — they would simply be elsewhere, vibrating at a frequency their eyes could not perceive.

E. Gadd validated this hypothesis with the specific enthusiasm of a scientist encountering a student who has independently arrived at a correct conclusion without knowing the relevant literature. The logic held: a localized dimensional pocket would explain the acoustic void, the heavy air Luigi was feeling, the clean emptiness.

Leo's follow-up: if it was a bubble, they had to pop it.

E. Gadd's follow-up: not like that.

But the direction was correct. Find the pin. Find the epicenter of the distortion. Find the point where the interference was strongest. Disrupt the frequency. Reintegrate with the primary dimension.

Leo found a pin in his pocket.

Luigi said he was going to resign.

E. Gadd produced the Ionic Disruptor-Z.

Leo took it. Leo handed it to Luigi.

## What Leo Said to Luigi


Waluigi is going to document this moment with complete attention because it is the most significant thing that happened on the train on the first night, and it happened quietly, in a dark carriage, with a pulsating void nearby and Luigi holding a device he was certain would kill him.

Luigi had been in this carriage for hours being afraid. The fear was specific and documented and coherent: he knew what ghosts were, he knew what dimensional instability was, he knew what happened to people who stood too close to localized singularities. His fear was not irrational. His fear was the correct response to accurate information about real danger.

But Luigi had been retreating from the fear rather than working with it. He had been describing the danger in exhaustive detail and then waiting for someone else to resolve it. He had been making himself small — literally, physically smaller, pulling his knees up, huddling in corners, pulling his cap over his eyes. The man who had faced Bowser alongside Mario, who had operated as Agent L, who had infiltrated Aegis Command successfully enough that the Legion felt it necessary to chemically lobotomize him to prevent him from doing it again — that man was not currently present in the carriage. What was present was the shell of him, performing his fear rather than working through it.

Leo handed Luigi the Ionic Disruptor-Z. And then Leo said:

It's not that you can't. You must. Just because Mario is missing and Peach is dead doesn't mean you can be a shell of your former self. I read the news. I know the truth. You are bigger and better than that. Be brave.

Waluigi wants to document several things about this statement.

First: Leo read the news. Leo knew about Peach before boarding this train. Leo knew about Mario's absence. Leo came into this mission with existing knowledge about Luigi's context — the assassination, the disappearance, the specific weight that Luigi is carrying — and had been watching Luigi operate under that weight for the entire night before saying anything about it.

Second: 'just because Mario is missing and Peach is dead doesn't mean you can be a shell of your former self.' This is not a gentle statement. This is not reassurance. This is someone identifying the behavior — being a shell — and naming it directly in front of the person exhibiting it. Leo did not soften it. Leo did not say 'I know this is hard' or 'you're doing your best.' Leo said: this is what you're doing, and it is not who you are.

Third: 'I read the news. I know the truth.' Waluigi is holding this carefully because it implies Leo knows something about Luigi that Luigi has not disclosed during this trip. The truth about what? About the Vigilance operation? About Agent L? About what happened during the Mr. L period? About Peach's assassination specifically? Leo's knowledge of 'the truth' is not specified, and its unspecified nature is significant — Luigi does not know what Leo knows. Luigi cannot assess how much Leo knows. The statement opens a question that the dimensional void interrupted before it could be answered.

Fourth: 'be brave.' Not 'be fearless.' Not 'stop being scared.' Be brave. Bravery is what you do when you are afraid and you go anyway. Leo was not asking Luigi to stop being afraid. Leo was asking Luigi to go anyway.

Waluigi does not know what Luigi's response was. The record ends at the statement. The void was pulsating. The Ionic Disruptor-Z was in Luigi's hands. The sentence had been spoken and it was sitting in the carriage between them, waiting to see what Luigi would do with it.

Waluigi is documenting this as an unresolved moment of significant operational and personal weight. The void can wait. The dimensional pocket can wait. What happens in the next thirty seconds — what Luigi does with a statement that just named the thing he has been doing and told him to stop — is what this section of the record is actually about. Waluigi is continuing the documentation of the Maglev Express's first night because the second and third movements of this sequence contain things that the first movement established and that the rest of the mission will depend on. The void is resolved.

The train is moving.

Two new variables have attached themselves to the party.

None of this was in E.

Gadd's original briefing, which contained maps, ghost classifications, Poltergust calibration schedules, and sleep recommendations, and did not contain Stone, the Knight, a dimensional pocket, or the specific conversation that happened in the dark before Luigi fired the Disruptor-Z.

Waluigi wants to document that conversation first, because it is the pivot point that everything else in this record depends on.

## Luigi Fires the Ionic Disruptor-Z


Leo handed Luigi the Ionic Disruptor-Z. And then Leo said: it's not that you can't. You must. Just because Mario is missing and Peach is dead doesn't mean you can be a shell of your former self. I read the news. I know the truth. You are bigger and better than that. Be brave.

The record of what happened next begins with Luigi's shoulders slumping. The manic terror in his eyes fading into a hollow sadness. A single tear tracking through the grime on his cheek.

Mario. He whispered the name. He looked at the floor. His lower lip trembled. Everything is gone wrong, isn't it. The kingdom. My brother. Everything feels like it's just drifting away into that dark thing.

Waluigi wants to document Luigi's response to his own name being spoken here, because 'a shell' is not a gentle characterization. Leo did not soften it. He identified the behavior — retreating, describing danger instead of facing it, waiting for someone else to make the decisive move — and named it directly in front of the person exhibiting it. Luigi heard it as the truth it was. He did not deny it. He did not argue. He clutched the Disruptor-Z to his chest and said: I can't let it end like this. I can't just stay in the corner while everything falls apart.

He said he would try. He said it with the specific emotional honesty of someone who is not promising success but is promising the attempt. He gripped the canister with both hands. He braced his elbows against his sides to steady the tremor in his arms. He took one slow, agonizingly careful step toward the center of the carriage. His eyes locked on the heart of the pulsating darkness.

But if I accidentally turn us into stardust, he said, I'm going to be very, very cross with you.

Waluigi finds this line important. Not because it is funny, though it is, but because of what it demonstrates about Luigi's emotional architecture in this moment. He is still afraid. The fear is still there, fully present, fully documented. He is making a joke about dying. The joke is how Luigi holds fear without being consumed by it — he names the worst outcome, he makes it small enough to say out loud, and then he goes anyway.

Leo said: show the world why you are number one.

Luigi stared at Leo's face for a long beat, looking for mockery and finding none. He let out a breath that sounded like a deflating balloon. He looked at the Poltergust on his back. He looked at the Disruptor-Z. The weight of both felt different. Less like a burden. More like tools.

Number one, he repeated. He wiped his nose with his sleeve. He stood slightly straighter. He said: I don't even know if I can be number zero-point-five. But I can't just sit here and wait for the dark to swallow us whole.

He took a deep breath. He planted his feet on the vibrating floorboards. He pointed the nozzle toward the swirling purple rift. He gritted his teeth. He let out a sound far more heroic than he probably felt and lunged forward toward the edge of the void.

HIIII-YAAAA.

Waluigi is going to be precise about what the HIIII-YAAAA represents in this record. It is not bravery in the absence of fear. Luigi was terrified. The fear is documented across the entire preceding sequence — the chattering teeth, the whimpering, the retreating to corners, the description of running until his legs fell off. The HIIII-YAAAA happened while all of that was still present. It happened despite it. This is what Leo meant by be brave. Not the absence of fear. The decision to go anyway, with a battle cry, while still being afraid.

The Poltergust drew in the volatile energy from the rift. The suction pulled at Luigi's cap. His boots skidded against the floorboards. The purple light spiraled into the nozzle. A vortex of crackling electricity and swirling shadows.

I won't let you down, Luigi shouted. And definitely won't let the Professor lose his precious machine.

The air around the nozzle warped. The heat caused the atmosphere to shimmer. The light turned incandescent white, pulsing with Luigi's heartbeat. Then — a sound like a massive glass pane shattering. Then silence. One heartbeat of absolute nothing.

Luigi stood frozen. The nozzle glowing with dull pulsing heat. A strange swirling mist of white and violet particles spiraling into the canister.

He looked back at Leo over his shoulder, pale and drenched in sweat. He asked if it was over. He asked without knowing the answer. He asked while still bracing the nozzle, unwilling to lower it until confirmed.

Leo looked around. The people had not come back. The train was still stopped.

Waluigi notes: Luigi acted correctly and the void collapsed and the dimensional pocket was resolved and the train was still at Blackwood Junction. The void was the pin. The resolution of the void did not automatically restart everything. This is important operational information and also important character information: Luigi did the brave thing and the brave thing was not immediately rewarded with safety. The station was still dark. The carriages were still empty. The victory was real and the danger continued. Luigi had done what Leo asked and the world had not immediately become easier.

He held the nozzle anyway.

## Stone and the Knight: What


They Are and What They Want

Stone and his companion were in the carriage when the party came through. The companion — subsequently designated the Knight by the record, though the Knight has declined to confirm this or any other name — had been watching the gap beneath the baggage compartment door with the focused attention of someone who expects what is on the other side to come through it. Stone had been pacing with the specific energy of someone who is bored and dangerous and accustomed to both.

The encounter began as a confrontation. Guns raised. Legion insignia on Stone's gear, though Stone has since clarified his relationship with the Legion in terms that distance him from institutional loyalty while retaining his operational style: the Legion taught him to spot opportunity. The Legion's values are order and control. Stone's values are survival and payment. These overlap frequently enough that the distinction may be academic.

Waluigi wants to document Stone's analysis of the current political landscape because it was delivered without being asked for and contains more useful intelligence than E. Gadd's pre-mission briefing:

The Legion is in decline. Stone called it stabilizing, but the word choice is the word choice of someone who knows the honest assessment and has selected the more flattering framing. The old ways were built on absolute unyielding order. Now it's chaos and containment. Everyone scrambling for whatever scrap of power is left floating. The regime is just a word people use when they want to feel like someone is still in charge.

On the Mages Guild: glorified parlor tricksters who think they can rewrite reality with chanted syllables and glowing dust. Magic is just another weapon. Messy, unpredictable. Unlike a well-forged shield or a disciplined legion, you can't see its edge until it's already cutting through your throat. They play with fire and he prefers to be the one holding the extinguisher.

Waluigi is filing both assessments as primary intelligence. Stone is not a neutral observer — he has operational history with the Legion and active distrust of the Guild. But biased assessments from people with direct experience are often more useful than neutral assessments from people without it. Stone has seen both institutions fail. His descriptions of their failure modes are specific and credible.

The tactical realignment — Stone's phrase, deliberately chosen to avoid words like 'change of heart' or 'cooperation' — was not offered from goodwill. It was offered from calculation. Stone identified Leo, Luigi, and E. Gadd as assets who were either going to be the reason the train reached its destination or the reason it ended up at the bottom of a ravine. He preferred to be on the surviving side. He offered temporary service, explicitly not friendship, explicitly not alliance. A service contract with a defined scope: keep them from getting their heads taken off.

Waluigi respects the honesty of this framing. Temporary service with explicit terms and no pretense of loyalty is more reliable than offered friendship with unstated conditions. Stone's contract is legible. Waluigi can work with legible.

The Knight is less legible.

Names are for those who intend to be remembered, the Knight said. I am simply what I need to be to ensure the objective is met.

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing this statement and has arrived at the following: it is either a genuine philosophy about identity and operational necessity, a trained deflection response that reveals nothing while sounding profound, or the specific posture of someone whose name would be recognized and who has decided recognition is a liability. All three possibilities are consistent with the available evidence. Waluigi cannot determine which is operative.

What Waluigi can determine: the Knight is competent in ways that Stone's competence does not overlap with. Stone is loud and effective. Stone announces himself, occupies space, makes his confidence part of his operational presence. The Knight is quiet in the specific way of someone who has trained to be quiet as a tactical choice. When Stone said whatever is hitting those couplings isn't a mechanical failure, he said it to the room. When the Knight moved to stabilize the conduit during the engine repair, they moved without announcing the intention. They acted. The action was the communication.

The Knight's stated objective — survival of the mission parameters, identification and neutralization of anomalies that cannot be allowed to reach their destination — is vague in ways that are either honest about the nature of their assignment or deliberately designed to avoid commitment to specifics. Waluigi does not know which anomalies. Waluigi does not know which destination. Waluigi does not know whose mission parameters are being referenced. The Knight did not elaborate and Leo did not press.

Leo's response was: close enough. My objective is to start this damn Maglev Express.

Waluigi notes that Leo has not disclosed the Clockwork Spire as a destination to either Stone or the Knight. Leo held this information internally while working alongside both of them through the engine repair sequence. This is the correct operational decision. Stone has identified them as assets but has not disclosed his own full agenda. The Knight has not disclosed theirs. Mutual partial disclosure is the appropriate equilibrium for a temporary alliance formed in a ghost-infested train car at midnight.

## The Walk to the Control Hub: What the Empty Carriages Contained


The route from the passenger carriages to the Main Control Hub produced evidence that the Blackwood Junction stop was not simple mechanical failure. E. Gadd's assessment — confirmed by his specter-scope readings — was ectoplasmic condensation settling on the upholstery like frost, the specific clean emptiness of a dimensional pocket rather than the messy evidence of violence or flight. One child-sized shoe in the aisle. No blood. No disrupted seating. No snack wrappers.

The next carriage contained walls coated in a thick translucent layer of pulsating violet ectoplasm. A heavy metal luggage crate vibrating violently on the floor, something beneath it punching upward rhythmically. A toad-shaped silhouette that rippled when illuminated, its edges blurring toward the ceiling. Waluigi notes: the toad-shaped silhouette was not a toad. It was a lure, or a residual impression, or a manifestation of the void's content-filling capacity — empty spaces in dimensional pockets sometimes populate themselves with echoes of what was most recently present. Passengers. Toads. Shapes.

Luigi identified the light as a potential traversal mechanism. Leo tested the hypothesis: the residue receded slightly from direct light, the light acting as a repellent. E. Gadd's objection that you cannot walk on photons is technically correct. E. Gadd's subsequent acknowledgment that the light might induce temporary photo-polymerization in the ectoplasm — momentarily hardening the surface — is the more operationally relevant observation. The carriages were navigated. The sludge was cleared using Luigi's dark light and Leo's improvised spectral-lens technique. The path to the control hub was opened.

Singing was heard during the carriage navigation.

Seems our regime has plummeted south. Don't need to scream if you don't have a mouth. Why bite the hand that feeds when it's the only hand you're getting. It's time to see that this great train is the only place you're ever going to be. So strap in, take it on the chin, and don't forget who is running the show.

This was Stone and his companion. The singing was either a communication of genuine institutional disillusionment set to melody, a territorial marker designed to test the response of whatever was in the carriages, or Stone's particular brand of psychological warfare adapted to the specific acoustics of an empty train car at midnight. The lyrical content — regime plummeting, no screaming without a mouth, this train as the only permanent place — maps directly onto Stone's subsequent analysis of the Legion's decline. The singing was Stone thinking out loud in the medium of someone who has decided that thinking out loud loudly is preferable to silence in a haunted space.

Waluigi files the song and its lyrics as Stone's operational philosophy expressed in music. The relevant line for understanding Stone: why bite the hand that feeds when it's the only hand you're getting. Stone's pragmatism is not cynicism about values. It is a calculated relationship with power. You align with the hand that feeds. You do not bite it. You assess when the hand stops feeding and you realign. The hand that was feeding — the Legion's order and certainty — has plummeted south. Stone is currently in the process of finding the next hand.

The door opened. Guns raised. Leo did not flinch. The standoff produced the tactical realignment. The party moved forward.

## The Engine Room: All Five Pull the Lever


The Main Control Hub is the structural brain of the Maglev Express. Amber flickering from a central command console. Dozens of holographic displays showing scrambled telemetry and red error messages. Walls lined with heavy-duty conduits pulsing like veins. A single large lever prominently positioned among unresponsive buttons and flickering dials. A warning light spinning rapidly, casting red strobe light.

Leo's assessment upon arrival: I have no idea what any of this is. Well, might as well flip this lever that says FORWARD. The train must move on.

Waluigi notes: Leo's assessment and his proposed action are both correct. The assessment is honest — he does not understand the system. The action is correct — the system needs to be started and the forward lever is the starting mechanism. The combination of honest incomprehension and direct action is Leo's consistent operational style across the entire night. He does not pretend to understand things he does not understand. He acts on the information he has. He asks E. Gadd to work his magic when E. Gadd's expertise is the appropriate tool. He pulls people into helping when more hands are needed.

The engine repair sequence required contributions from all five parties present:

E. Gadd provided the technical knowledge — the secondary intake valves, the spectral resonance tuner, the containment seals, the pressure gauges, the mana-stabilization array, the localized subspace rupture risk if the resonance hit the breaking point. Without E. Gadd's knowledge the lever would have been pulled without the manifold stabilized and the outcome would have been as he described: catastrophic.

Leo provided physical stabilization and coordination — holding the resonance tuner at 440 hertz while E. Gadd worked the valves, planting his feet against the vibration, calling for more hands when more hands were needed, directing the sequence without pretending to lead the technical elements. Knowing what you do not know and routing around it is a form of operational intelligence that Waluigi finds undervalued.

Luigi provided the Poltergust suction to pull escaping violet mist back into the canister — a specific contribution that required him to move toward the machinery rather than away from it. He moved toward it. He held the suction steady while telling Leo he was going to be vaporized if it popped. He held the suction anyway. This is the same mechanism as the HIIII-YAAAA: stating the worst outcome and going anyway.

The Knight held the structural conduit under immense pressure — bracing armored shoulders against the leaking pipe and providing the physical anchor that allowed E. Gadd and Leo to work without the junction buckling. No announcement. No request for acknowledgment. The pipe needed holding. The Knight held it. Steady was the only word spoken.

Stone held the perimeter and identified the threat pattern — noting that the rhythmic thudding against the coupling was deliberate, not mechanical. We need to finish this before that thing finds a way inside. Stone's contribution was awareness of the external threat while the others were occupied with the internal one. A person watching the door while the engine is being repaired is doing something essential. Stone did it without being asked.

All five pulled the lever.

The mechanism resisted. The gears screamed. Luigi's face turned red. E. Gadd's spectacles nearly left his face. The Knight's armored shoulders strained. Leo planted his feet. Stone added his weight.

CLACK. The lever hit its locked position.

The thrum began in the belly of the train. Blue-white light surging through the fuel lines. The train lurching forward. The wheels grinding against the tracks with newfound ferocity. The violet mist swirling back toward the primary intake valves as the pressure stabilized.

E. Gadd screamed that the conductivity was stabilizing, that the kinetic input had successfully re-engaged the spectral dampeners, that they were moving through the dark.

Luigi collapsed backward against the control panel. A shaky, breathless laugh. The speedometer climbing.

Leo thought: next stop, the Clockwork Spire. He did not say it out loud. The cards remained private.

## Blackwood Junction to Normality:


The Return of the Passengers

The transition from dimensional pocket to primary dimension produced a specific sensory sequence that Waluigi's sources describe consistently: jarring brightness, the clinical glare of Mages Guild magical lanterns replacing the suffocating violet, mundane sounds returning simultaneously — tea sets, conversation, the clicking of heels on polished wood. The passengers who had been dimensionally displaced were suddenly present. The conductor appeared. The lights came back on. The train was populated again.

The horror was over in the specific way that dimensional horrors end: not gradually, but all at once, replaced by complete ordinariness. People sitting in seats where a void had been. Tea cups on tables near where the ectoplasm had pooled. The Mages Guild personnel moving through the carriages with the practiced efficiency of people who have decided not to acknowledge the last several hours.

A Toad appeared. The Toad stared at the five of them — Leo, Luigi, E. Gadd, Stone, and the Knight — standing in the engine room. The Toad wanted to know why they were in the engine room.

Waluigi finds the Toad's question the most honest moment in the entire sequence. Everything else in this night has been dimensional voids, spectral catapults, Legion singing, improvised manifold repairs, and a lever that says FORWARD being pulled by five people who had varying levels of understanding of what it did. The Toad's question is simply: why are you in the engine room.

The Knight said: a simple mechanical complication.

Waluigi notes the Knight's chosen cover story with specific attention. They did not hesitate. They did not look to Stone or Leo for guidance. A simple mechanical complication is the sentence of someone who has produced cover stories before, who knows that the simplest explanation requires the least defense, and who has calibrated exactly how much detail is needed to satisfy a Toad asking a standard question in a repopulated train car.

The Knight has done this before. Whatever this is — the missions, the objectives, the silent competence — this is not new.

Stone did not contradict the cover story. Leo did not elaborate on it. Luigi was presumably still breathing heavily and trying to look like someone who had simply been examining engine machinery for reasonable professional reasons.

E. Gadd's response to the situation was not recorded in the available sources. Waluigi suspects it involved either a lengthy technical explanation that inadvertently supported the cover story through incomprehensibility, or an indignant harrumph followed by retreating to his specter-scope.

## What This Night Has Established


The first night of the Maglev Express transit has produced the following operational developments that will affect everything that follows:

Luigi is not a shell. He was a shell for most of the night. He stopped being a shell when Leo named the behavior and asked him to stop. The HIIII-YAAAA happened. The void collapsed. Luigi held the suction in the engine room while telling Leo he was going to be vaporized. The man who infiltrated Aegis Command, who was chemically lobotomized by the Legion because he was too effective to leave operational, who went silent when asked if Mr. L did something evil — that man is still present. He is afraid and he is present. The Clockwork Spire is still three days away. Whatever is waiting at the manor will require both.

Stone and the Knight are aboard. Stone's terms are explicit: temporary service, not friendship, calibrated by survival. The Knight's terms are: objectives aligned as long as the threats are the same threats. Both of these relationships are functional and limited and will remain so until either the objectives diverge or the threats change. Waluigi is watching for both.

Leo has not disclosed the destination to either of them. This is correct.

The Mages Guild's dimensional pocket at Blackwood Junction is resolved but not explained. Something caused it. The cargo crate that was vibrating from something underneath it was not examined after the void collapsed. The thing hitting the coupling from outside was identified by Stone as deliberate but was not identified further. The dimensional pocket that displaced all passengers except the five who resolved it was not explained by anyone. These are open threads. The Clockwork Spire is three days away. The train is moving. The threads are being carried aboard.

E. Gadd wanted three days to prepare. He has three days. He will not spend them calmly. He will spend them checking gauges, analyzing the residue samples he almost certainly collected during the cleaning operation, and muttering about hullabaloos. This is E. Gadd preparing. It is adequate preparation if it produces the technical knowledge needed at the manor. It will be loud.

Luigi needs to sleep. Whether Luigi will sleep is a separate question from whether Luigi needs to. The answer to the first question is probably no. The answer to the second question is yes.

Leo needs dinner. He checked the menu at the beginning of the night. He has not eaten. The Mages Guild transport presumably has a dining car. Whether the dining car survived the dimensional pocket intact enough to still be serving is undocumented.

Waluigi hopes so. The Clockwork Spire is three days away. A person who has just pulled a spectral entity through a ceiling with a vacuum, patched a structural breach with green sealant, negotiated a tactical realignment with an Iron Legion-adjacent mercenary, fired an Ionic Disruptor-Z through a dimensional void, repaired a train manifold at midnight, and pulled a lever marked FORWARD with four other people while something hit the coupling from outside deserves a meal.

WAH.
